name: Nucleus
short_description: The cell's archive and control room: a spherical organelle bounded by a DOUBLE membrane (two lipid bilayers with a perinuclear space between them, continuous with the rough ER), pierced by thousands of octagonal nuclear pore complexes, holding the genome as peripheral heterochromatin and central euchromatin around a membrane-less nucleolus that builds ribosomes.

textbook.1: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; strong start - a clear double-line envelope band studded with dozens of amber octagonal pore rings runs all the way round, dense purple heterochromatin hugs the whole periphery against a paler lavender-veined euchromatin interior, a bounded-free reddish nucleolus sits off-centre, muted educational palette, thin outlines, dark charcoal ground, no text, no border. The one miss: the attached rough-ER protrusion on the right is drawn as plain parallel membrane lines with no ribosome dots, so it reads as more envelope rather than ER and the continuity point is muddled. Fix-prompt: the attached ER sheets must be visibly stippled with dark ribosome dots on their outer surface so the smooth-envelope-vs-studded-ER contrast is unmistakable)
textbook.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; same strong composition, ER fix applied - the protrusion is now clearly stippled with small dark ribosome dots along its full length, obviously continuous with, and distinct in texture from, the smooth double-line nuclear envelope. Double membrane intact everywhere with the perinuclear-space gap visible, thousands of amber pore rings evenly scattered, nuclear lamina implied as a dashed inner line, heterochromatin correctly peripheral and denser, euchromatin correctly central and looser, nucleolus a boundary-free denser patch, no X-shaped chromosomes, no nucleoid, no cell wall, no text, no border. Used as the primary labelled figure)

sem.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; does not read as SEM at all - a soft, painterly, near-abstract composition (more like stylised concept art than a microscopy plate) with a smooth toy-like sphere in the centre that could be misread as an odd inclusion, an amber pore field pattern on one facet that is nice in isolation but not photorealistic, and a cross-section edge that never resolves into two distinct membrane surfaces with a visible gap - the double-membrane requirement is not met. Fix-prompt: demand grainy, high-contrast, real-SEM-plate photorealism with harsh directional lighting and a torn fracture surface; make the double wall unmistakable at the cut edge; make the nucleolus a denser fractured texture, not a smooth toy sphere)
sem.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; a convincing false-colour freeze-fracture SEM plate now - a torn cross-section edge on the left shows two clearly separate, parallel membrane surfaces with a dark gap between them (the perinuclear space), continuing directly into a stack of ribosome-studded rough-ER sheets at the frame edge; a few small pore profiles with raised rims sit in the torn wall; the broken-open interior on the right is a coarse granular fracture texture (chromatin) with one smooth, denser, rounded amber-tan lobe (the nucleolus, no membrane, correctly just a denser fracture face); grainy high-contrast surface detail, shallow depth of field, cool studio lighting, dark uncluttered ground, no text, no border. Not labelled (SEM is the surface/fracture comparison plate, consistent with project convention)

3d.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image, accepted on the first attempt; a wedge-cut sphere clearly shows two separate, concentric, translucent membrane shells with a visible gap between them running the whole cut edge, studded with dozens of glowing amber octagonal pore rings; a fine dark mesh (nuclear lamina) lines the inner shell with grape-like clusters of dusty-purple heterochromatin pressed against it all around the rim, a lighter lavender euchromatin of loose looping fibres filling the centre, and one smooth terracotta-orange nucleolus with no boundary of its own. At the left, a stack of ribosome-studded rough-ER sheets (visible black ribosome beads) is clearly continuous with the outer shell, not just adjacent to it. Natural believable biological tints, soft global illumination, subsurface scattering, clean dark studio ground, edge to edge, single specimen, no X-shaped chromosomes, no nucleoid, no cell wall, no text, no border. Used for the labelled figure)

watercolor.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image, accepted on the first attempt; warm aged paper fills the frame edge to edge and corner to corner with a soft blue-grey wash halo directly on the paper - no mat, frame, drop shadow or sheet-on-a-surface. Two concentric ink-outlined membrane circles with a pale paper gap between them ring the whole organelle, studded with amber pore-ring motifs; a fine cross-hatch mesh just inside the inner line stands in for the nuclear lamina; dense purple cloud-clumps of heterochromatin hug the whole periphery against a lighter lavender scatter of euchromatin dashes in the centre; one smooth orange-red nucleolus sits off-centre with no ink outline of its own; a stippled grey-blue rough-ER cluster at the lower right connects by a fine line directly into the outer membrane circle. Fine ink linework over soft translucent washes, no text, no arrows, no scale bar. Used for the labelled figure (black-on-paper ink per style convention))

reference: pass, with an honest caveat (Wikimedia Commons "Pancreatic acinar cells - TEM.jpg", Public domain, Louisa Howard, Rippel Electron Microscope Facility, Dartmouth College, JEOL 100CX TEM - the same trusted source already used for this set's Golgi-apparatus plate. A genuine thin-section transmission electron micrograph unmistakably showing a cell nucleus: a large, roughly kidney-shaped body with a smooth continuous envelope contour, its interior a textbook-clear mottled pattern of dark, electron-dense heterochromatin clumps against paler, open euchromatin. Crucially, dense ribosome-studded rough-ER sheets crowd the cytoplasm at upper-right and lower-left and visibly run up to, and merge with, the nuclear envelope - the ER-envelope continuity that is this organelle's single most commonly missed teaching point is directly visible here, in real electron microscopy, not just asserted. Caveat stated honestly: at this magnification the two envelope membranes are not individually resolved as two separate lines (they read as one contour - the ~20-50 nm perinuclear space is below this plate's resolution/contrast), and no nucleolus happens to be in frame; both are compensated for explicitly by the illustrated styles, which draw the double membrane and the nucleolus as first-class labelled structures. Cleaned with a plain DETERMINISTIC CROP, not edit_image.py: the raw 640x480 download's baked-in footer band (500 nm scale bar, '1Pancreas', '1/7/0 REMF' instrument text) was cropped away, the remaining 640x455 content centre-cropped to a 455x455 square, then upscaled 2.37x to 1080x1080 with LANCZOS - stated explicitly per instructions. No pixels invented or re-illustrated, only crop + resize)
decision: use as final and as the primary labelled figure; attempt 1 on gemini-2.5-flash-image was let down only by an unstudded ER protrusion (looked like extra envelope, not ER); attempt 2 fixed that with an explicit ribosome-dot instruction and passed clean on the same model, no escalation needed

use as final; attempt 1 on gemini-2.5-flash-image failed outright - painterly/abstract, no resolved double-membrane cross-section, toy-like nucleolus; attempt 2 with an explicit real-SEM-plate/fracture-photorealism rewrite passed clean on the same model (Nano Banana), no escalation to Nano Banana Pro needed. Not labelled, per project convention for the SEM surface/fracture plate

use as final on the first attempt; labelled figure built. Double-shell envelope with visible gap, pore rings, lamina mesh, heterochromatin/euchromatin contrast, boundary-free nucleolus and ribosome-studded ER continuity all correct together on gemini-2.5-flash-image

use as final on the first attempt; labelled figure built with black-on-paper ink. Full-bleed aged paper, double membrane with visible gap, pore motifs, chromatin contrast, boundary-free nucleolus and ER continuity all correct on gemini-2.5-flash-image, no escalation needed
